patch_description: The previous program failed because it returned an empty `column_orderings` list (`return final_df, []`), violated its own shape assertions (it added an `original_index` helper column, merged discarded columns back with a merge that changes row order, and mis-handled `col_merge`), used a slow pandas/threaded recursion whose row-reordering broke row identity, and never optimized the actual objective (serialized character-Trie prefix reuse). The fix replaces the whole editable block with a clean, bounded construction: factorize cell strings once; build up to three candidate per-row column orderings (a global frequency/length-ranked order, a length-weighted variant, and a recursive conditional partition tree over factorized codes); score each candidate exactly with the sorted-string adjacent-LCP sum (C-speed slice-equality binary search); return the best candidate's per-row orderings along with the untouched dataframe (rows and cell values preserved, object dtype, NaN cells intact). `col_merge` groups are treated as atomic ordering units so merged columns stay contiguous, and `row_stop`/`col_stop` bound recursion depth. No columns are added or dropped, no cells altered, and every row keeps its identity, so validation of shape, data, and ordering consistency passes.
